key_insight: Maxwell symmetries can be turned into exact transformations of scattering parameters, enabling data augmentation and equivariant neural networks for electromagnetic surrogate modeling.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce the number of expensive simulations needed to train accurate models for photonic and electromagnetic device design while preserving physical consistency.
method: Derive symmetry-to-scattering transformation rules from the equivariance of Maxwell's equations.
Use these rules for systematic data augmentation in training datasets.
Build exactly equivariant neural networks for both discrete and continuous symmetry groups.
evidence_signal: On photonic-crystal slabs and free-form diffraction gratings, symmetry-informed models improved data efficiency by about an order of magnitude, while equivariant models enforced physical constraints exactly.
watch_item: The approach depends on correctly identifying and encoding the relevant device symmetries, which may be nontrivial for complex geometries or imperfect fabrication.
paper_title: Symmetry-Informed Deep Learning for Electromagnetic Scattering
